study.title: Different brain responses to electro-acupuncture and moxibustion treatment in patients with Crohn's disease
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial; resting-state fMRI before and after 12-week treatment; comparison with healthy controls
study.randomization: Equally and randomly assigned; process was blind, serially-coded, and confidential
study.blinding: Different groups of CD patients were assigned to different isolated rooms for treatment and were blind to the setup of the study; evaluators performing statistical analyses were blind
study.population: Patients with Crohn's disease in remission and healthy controls
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) 18–50 years old; (2) more than 6 years of education; (3) remission period lasting 12 months or longer; (4) CDAI score ≤ 150; (5) CDEIS score <3; (6) dominant right hand; (7) no acupuncture treatment in the last three months
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) C reactive protein >10mg/L; erythrocyte sedimentation rate >20mm/h; platelets >300×10^9/L; (2) CD patients who suffered from abdominal fistula, sinus or had CD-related abdominal surgery; (3) patients who received glucocorticoids, anti TNF-α drugs or other biological agents, mental or opioid drugs in the past 3 months; (4) pregnant or lactating women; (5) patients with current or previous history of mental and nervous system disease or head trauma and loss of consciousness; (6) claustrophobic patients; (7) those with metal implants in the body; additionally for treatment arms: those taking immunosuppressive drugs in the past 3 months

arms.dropouts: 1 patient demonstrated head movements during the scan; 1 was unable to complete scans due to schedule conflicts
All 18 patients underwent fMRI scans after treatment, which returned useful results
12 patients excluded for taking azathioprine; 4 cases refused to receive acupuncture or moxibustion treatment

interventions.laterality_exact: ST25 bilateral; CV6 and RN12 midline
interventions.manipulation_exact: needles connected to a HANS electro-acupuncture apparatus (Model LH100A TENS, Nanjing, China); two conducting ends connected to ST25 and CV6 at left-hand side, and ST25 and RN12 at right-hand side
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: three times a week for 12 weeks, totaling up to 36 treatment sessions
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: acupuncture points chosen in reference to prior research, typical for the treatment of gastrointestinal diseases

interventions.stimulation_type: heat stimulation via moxa cone on herbal cake placed on acupuncture point
interventions.laterality_exact: ST25 bilateral; CV6 and RN12 midline
interventions.manipulation_exact: Moxa cone placed on top of herbal cake and ignited for herbs-partitioned moxibustion on each acupuncture point every time. Herbal cake: Radix aconiti preparata, Coptis chinesis, Aucklandia Lappa, Carthamus tinctorius, Salvia miltiorrhiza and Angelica sinensis ground into fine powder, 2.8g dissolved in lukewarm water with malt sugar, shaped into herbal cake with 23mm diameter and 5mm thickness. Moxa cone: height 16mm, diameter 18mm (Han Medicine, Nanyang, China)

extraction_notes.note: Exact r values for Pearson correlation analyses between ReHo changes and CDAI score decreases are visible in Figure 3a but cannot be reliably read from the PDF text. The figure caption references specific r and p values for individual scatter plots. Individual numeric r values are not reported in the main text tables.

No sham acupuncture or placebo control arm was included. The authors acknowledge this as a limitation: 'One limitation of this study is the lack of a placebo-controlled group. Our placebo-controlled protocol was denied by the Institutional Review Board due to likely progression and recurrence of CD.' Expectancy, blinding success, and credibility were therefore not formally assessed.

Sensation/deqi measurement was not formally assessed or reported with any standardized instrument. The only mention of sensory response to moxibustion is narrative: 'Patients receiving moxibustion usually experience gratification and warmth.'
Adverse events were not explicitly reported in the paper. No adverse events section or statement about safety was found.

Table 4 footnote states *P<0.01 for within-group changes from baseline, but the text (Results section) states 'The CDAI scores of the two groups were significantly lower after treatment (P<0.001, P<0.001)'. There is a discrepancy between P<0.01 (table footnote) and P<0.001 (text). Both values are preserved as reported in their respective locations.

The total N enrolled is stated as 52 CD patients + 36 HCs = 88 total, but only 36 CD patients were randomized to treatment. The CD_all arm (n=52) was used for baseline imaging comparison with HCs. The treatment arms used a subset of 36 patients. The n_analyzed for imaging in the CD_all vs HC comparison appears to be 52+36=88, but this is not explicitly confirmed in the paper.

Table 5 contains one row for 'Parahippocampus/Hippocampus' in both EA (BA 20, -24 -21 -12, t=3.38, 10 voxels) and Mox groups, but the Mox group row has identical coordinates (-24 -21 -12) and no BA listed. This was extracted for the Mox group as separate row c005_r16, but the BA field was marked not_reported because Table 5 does not list a BA for the Mox Parahippocampus/Hippocampus row.

The paper uses 'CV6' and 'RN6' interchangeably to refer to the same acupoint (Qihai). In Figure 1 caption it is labeled RN6 (Qihai); in the intervention methods text it is called 'CV6'. Both are preserved as reported.

The n_analyzed_neuroimaging for the CD_all vs HC comparison was inferred as 52 (CD) + 36 (HC) = 88, based on enrollment numbers. The paper states 52 CD patients and 36 HCs were enrolled and all completed the image acquisition procedure. This value was recorded in the study-level field.

The paper does not report between-group comparisons of ReHo changes directly (EA vs Mox post-treatment comparison). The between-group analysis is described narratively as showing similar and different brain regions, visualized in Figure 3b and 3c, but no formal statistical table for the EA-vs-Mox contrast is provided.

For the moxibustion group, no session duration is explicitly given for each individual treatment session, unlike the EA group (30 minutes). The number of moxa cones per session or total burn time is not specified.
